$comment: INTEGRIQ DRAFT (native-data-gathering-provider, ported from spectr/connectors): Source and Job ship isEnabled false, per the requirement that a connector blocked on an unbuilt capability ships disabled. PARKED (Wave 3): the API needs a subscription key, referenced through the credential broker (credentialRef 'doffin'); no key ships. Unparked by its own change once the key is enrolled. ORIGINAL SPECTR NOTE: Phase-2 W3-revival OpenConnector ingestion config for Norway/Doffin, the 'revive-native (S-M)' verdict from README.md's W3 audit table. concurrentie-analyse/scripts/sync/sync_norway.py's own docstring documents the situation precisely: Doffin's Public API (Azure API Management, base betaapi.doffin.no/public/v2) is free but requires a self-service developer-portal signup (https://dof-notices-prod-api.developer.azure-api.net/ - create an account, subscribe to the 'Public API' product, copy the subscription key from Profile > Subscriptions) - this is 'Ruben territory' per the batch-3 task brief, not something obtainable inside an agent session, so this file ships as a DOCUMENTED DRAFT with the Job disabled. The subscription key itself lives in the OpenRegister credential broker (manifest-credentials-doffin change): the Source carries `credentialRef.credentialName: "doffin"` instead of any header-embedded key - the operator creates a credential named `doffin` (provider `doffin`) in Nextcloud user settings, allows app `openconnector`, and no secret or placeholder ever enters this repo. LIVE CONNECTIVITY CHECK (2026-07-06, within the ≤8-request budget - 2 requests used): a keyless GET against `https://betaapi.doffin.no/public/v2/notices?cpvCodes=48000000&pageNumber=1&pageSize=1` and a second attempt with an obviously-fake `Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key: fake-test-key-000` header both returned the identical `HTTP 404 {"statusCode":404,"message":"Resource not found"}` - confirming the host itself is alive and running a real Azure APIM gateway (the JSON error shape is APIM's own, matching the script's documented architecture), but NOT disambiguating why: Azure APIM's more typical unauthenticated-request response is `401 Access denied due to missing subscription key`, so a `404` here could mean either (a) APIM's route-masking hides even the existence of a path from a caller with no/invalid key, or (b) the exact `/public/v2/notices` path has moved since the Python script was written - its own docstring already flags the API as still-beta ('betaapi.doffin.no') and subject to change ('If it moves to production, update BASE_URL accordingly'). Neither can be resolved without a genuine subscription key, so the `sourceConfig.endpoint`/pagination shape below is carried over UNVERIFIED from the script's own documented contract (`GET /notices` with `cpvCodes`/`pageNumber`/`pageSize` query params, `{"notices":[...],"totalCount":N}` envelope) rather than confirmed against a real response - this is the one source in this batch whose field-level mapping was never checked against live data (the same class of gap as belgium.json's OAuth-gated mapping). Mapping mirrors sync_norway.py's own defensive multi-key fallback chains, since the script itself hedges against several possible eForms/REST field-naming variants it has apparently never pinned down either (`notice.get('title') or notice.get('noticeTitle') or notice.get('contractTitle')`, similarly for buyer/dates/CPV/value) - Twig's `|default()` chaining reproduces the same first-non-empty-wins logic. `extract_multilang()`'s language-preference logic (no/nb/nn/en) is approximated by chaining `.no`/`.nb`/`.nn`/`.en` attribute defaults - Twig's attribute access returns null (not an error) when the source value is a plain string rather than a dict, so the chain degrades safely either way, but - like the rest of this mapping - was never exercised against a real payload. `cpvCodes` uses the same scalar-to-array `cast` trick as latvia_iub.json/belgium.json (main CPV code only; the script's own `[cpv_main] + cpv_additional` array-union is not reproducible through Twig, see IMPORT.md). `estimatedValue` takes the first of three possible value-object shapes the script itself tries (`estimatedValue`/`totalValue`/`contractValue`), each of which may itself be a nested `{amount:...}` object or a bare number in the script's own handling - simplified here to the nested-object case only (`estimatedValue.amount`), the more eForms-idiomatic shape, since a single fixed dot-path cannot branch on the source value's own type the way the Python script's `isinstance()` check does. Job ships disabled - the secret blocker is resolved via the credential broker (`credentialRef`), so the ONLY remaining enablement blocker is live mapping verification: do not enable the Job until a real broker-held key has been used to check the mapping (and the 404-vs-401 route ambiguity) against at least one real response. One further simplification vs. the Python script: it loops over TWO CPV codes (48000000 software, 72000000 IT services) as two separate query passes; this Synchronization's `sourceConfig.query.cpvCodes` only wires the first (48000000) - OpenConnector has no multi-value-query-per-sync loop primitive, so covering both would need a second Source/Synchronization/Job triple (omitted here to keep the draft minimal; trivial to clone once the key is real and the shape is confirmed).

objects.name: Doffin (Norway public procurement portal)
objects.description: Norway's national procurement notice portal, via its Azure API Management-hosted Public API. Requires a free self-service developer-portal signup and subscription key (injected broker-side as the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header) - see this file's $comment for the signup path and the live connectivity check that could not fully disambiguate the API's current route shape without a real key. The subscription key is held by the OpenRegister credential broker, never in this config: this Source references it via `credentialRef.credentialName: "doffin"`. Operator recipe: in Nextcloud user settings -> Credentials, create a credential named `doffin` with provider `doffin`, paste the APIM subscription key there, and allow app `openconnector` (the sync engine is the calling app, not spectr). Mapping remains UNVERIFIED against a real response (404-vs-401 route ambiguity, see $comment) - the Job below stays disabled until a live check passes. Feeds the spectr `tender` register/schema via the norway-doffin-to-spectr-tender synchronization.
